pr_comments: Looks good, last thing just squash these 4 commits into one for less git spam :tada:

> Looks good, last thing just squash these 4 commits into one for less git spam 🎉

Done!

@nebkat 

This has been open for a few days, is there any action from me that is still needed before this can be merged ?

> @pedrolcn I am not a maintainer here, just helping out. There haven't been any merges in over a month so just a matter of waiting now. Approved by me anyway!

Oh, I didn't realize that, I see
Thanks for the response!

Thank you for your efforts!

However, why do we need this feature when we already have a `Index` decorator?
What you are suggesting is to introduce this:

```ts
@ManyToOne(() => Type, type => type.property, {
   option1: ... 
})
```

when we already have:

```ts
@Index({ option1: ... })
@ManyToOne(() => Type, type => type.property)
```

Don't see much of point. Next step would be to merge `@JoinColumn` into this decorator or even worse `@JoinTable`.

From my experience this kind of features only confuses people and complicates the code because of new flows in the code, e.g.:

* what if I put both `@Index({ someOptions })` and `@Index({ someOptions }) @ManyToOne({ index: otherOptions })`?
* user can ask what is the difference between putting index into `many-to-one` and separate index, needs additional documentation

> If you really want to solve the user confusion with these sort of things I think we need to move towards separate documentation and auto generated API reference. 

> I do agree that "many ways of doing the same thing" is a problem and one that TypeORM definitely suffers from (sometimes with subtle differences between them) and it can confuse users

I think you both admit that current design is confusing and I don't really want to continue with new features that bring a new confusion. Let me close it for now, until we have time to redesign current confusing things and make a better design.

## Feature Description

Add a quality-of-life indexing option to ManyToOne decorator.

### The Problem

<!--
  A clear and concise description of what the problem is, and
  why it needs to be implemented as a new feature for TypeORM.

  For example, "I'm always frustrated when ..."

  Why should this be a part of TypeORM?
-->

Not all RDBMSs auto-index the referencing-side of FKs (postgresql doesn't do it), and very frequently there are benefits of doing so. Since this ought to be a common idiom it makes sense for the ManyToOne decorator to accept an option which tell it to also create an index for the FK.

### The Solution

<!--
  A clear and concise description of what you want to happen.

  How can the requested feature be used to approach the problem it's supposed to solve?
-->

Add a `index?: boolean | IndexOptions & { name?: string }` property to ManyToOneRelations(a new interface which extends `RelationOptions`) which the decorator reads and creates the index metadata if it is set.
